correctness.rationale: Reconstructed over an arbitrary field of characteristic two. A^3=0 puts A^2 in the two-sided annihilator; noncommutativity needs at least two independent directions modulo A^2. Thus below dimension four only the three-dimensional, one-dimensional-square case can occur. For B=[[a,b],[c,d]], e=b+c≠0, multiplying by P=[[0,d/e],[a/e,1]] gives P^tB+BP=B, with no additional restriction on K or on det B. The projection onto the square is local: use that scaling derivation on the square and a central shear killing the square at each vector outside it. It violates Leibniz on a nonzero product of complement vectors. In the exhibited four-dimensional algebra det B=1; A²=Ann(A)=Kc and a hypothetical square-zero direct summand would sit inside the other summand's square. In the equation P^tB+BP=sB, entries (11),(21) kill p21,p32; (22),(23),(32) give p12=p23=s and p13=0; comparison of (13),(31) kills p23 and s. The remaining restrictions give a scalar diagonal and unrestricted p31. This gives exactly two quotient parameters and three independent central shears. The tests at y,z,y+z,x,x+y force precisely that quotient form even over F₂; locality also kills c. The two-local map is validated by extending prescribed values on two quotient vectors to a functional (homogeneity handles dependent inputs). Read verify.py and its saved transcript: the latter corroborates the 5/5 ranks over F₂,F₄,F₈ and 8,192,3584 lower-dimensional forms, but the replay of the displayed symbolic identities and pointwise argument above, not the finite script, is the proof for arbitrary fields. value.rationale: This gives the first possible noncommutative dimension within the stipulated characteristic-two two-step class, not just an isolated new multiplication table. The uniform smaller-dimension obstruction and the indecomposable witness identify why the familiar square-projection obstruction can stop working. The conclusion is not a classification at dimension four or a claim outside A³=0.
